A subsidiary in which the promoters hold 99.76% pre-issue, four product lines named in the filing, and six reporting periods of restated numbers — explained from the DRHP, page by page.

Do not infer an offer-for-sale leg. The digest names no selling shareholder, and the objects of the issue point to fresh capital for a plant, but the split is simply absent.

Two numbers on page 155 need care: 89,48,270 promoter shares and 99.76% of pre-issue capital, against paid-up capital of 89,70,000 shares on page 190. Report both as the filing states them.
The corporate promoter is both the seller's channel and a related party. Keep those two beats separate: one belongs in business, the other in governance and risks.
Treat the page 113 and page 45 'strengths' as the company's own framing. Attribute them to the filing rather than stating them as findings.

beats.beat: Processing specialty chemicals means buying mineral and chemical inputs and treating them so they do a specific job inside somebody else's product. The filing names four families — functional additives and chemically modified minerals (together its specialty chemicals), plus soft minerals and hard minerals — and one of its stated strengths is that these sell into a spread of end-user industries.
There is no order book described in the extracts. Sales are governed by purchase orders, not long-term or definitive customer agreements, which the filing lists as an internal risk factor.
The same is true on the buying side: no long-term agreements with raw material suppliers.

The channel is the parent. The company states it has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter to market and sell its products through that promoter's network, and lists 'support of our holding company' among its strengths.
Customer concentration is the sharpest number in this section: the top 10 customers accounted for around 59%, 57% and 59% of revenue from operations in FY2017, FY2016 and FY2015 respectively.
Exports exist but are small: ₹1,068.18 lakh over five years, to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka.

Footprint is manufacturing sites, not stores. Facilities sit at Plot 347 and Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and at Plot 104/3, Thenkasi Road, Pathur Village, Alangulam, Tirunelveli, Tamil Nadu, with administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur. None of those premises are owned by the company; the new Waghodia facility in the objects of the issue is a separate plot, 336.

The strengths the filing claims for itself — diversified product portfolio, diversified user industries, import substitution, support of the holding company, product innovation and R&D, and the management team — should be read as the company's own framing, not as tested results.

beats.beat: Scale first, because it frames everything else: this is a small company. Total assets were ₹34.25 crore at September 30, 2017, against paid-up equity capital of ₹8.97 crore.

The profit record has a shape: two loss years, then a turn. Loss of ₹0.27 crore in FY2013 and ₹0.12 crore in FY2014; profit of ₹1.50 crore in FY2015, ₹0.90 crore in FY2016 and ₹1.75 crore in FY2017; ₹1.33 crore in the six months to September 30, 2017.

Earnings per share tells the same story with different arithmetic: ₹(0.45) in FY2013, ₹(0.20) in FY2014, ₹2.47 in FY2015, ₹1.46 in FY2016, ₹2.43 in FY2017 and ₹1.48 for the six months to September 30, 2017.

Operating cash flow is the number to sit with. Net inflow was ₹2.01 crore in FY2013, ₹1.28 crore in FY2014, ₹4.22 crore in FY2015 and ₹8.03 crore in FY2016 — then an outflow of ₹3.50 crore in FY2017. The filing lists the negative cash flows of previous financial years as an internal risk factor in its own right.

Total assets moved ₹30.19 crore (FY2013), ₹26.79 crore (FY2014), ₹25.93 crore (FY2015), ₹27.67 crore (FY2016), ₹32.74 crore (FY2017), ₹34.25 crore (September 30, 2017) — a dip for two years, then a rebuild.
Contingent liabilities and commitments, to the extent not provided for, aggregated ₹29.11 lakh as at September 30, 2017.
Capital structure at September 30, 2017: authorised share capital ₹2,000.00 lakh and issued, subscribed and paid-up capital ₹897.00 lakh, represented by 89,70,000 equity shares of ₹10 each.

What is missing and must be said to be missing: revenue from operations, EBITDA, and borrowings or debt levels are not in the extracted facts. Customer-concentration percentages are expressed against 'revenue from operations', but no revenue figure accompanies them.

beats.beat: Four promoters are named: Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh and Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and the corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited.

Ownership before the issue is close to total: promoters hold 89,48,270 equity shares, or 99.76% of pre-issue paid-up equity, and the promoter group excluding promoters holds a further 21,510 shares, or 0.24%. Effectively none of the equity is held outside the promoter family and its companies today.

Related party transactions have existed in each of the last five financial years and in the six months to September 30, 2017, and the filing says they may continue. It also flags the whole category as an internal risk.
The company does not own the premises it operates from — two of the manufacturing sites and the administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur are on premises it does not own.
It has not registered its corporate logo, so it may be unable to stop others using it.

The compliance record has gaps: the filing admits instances of non-filing, incorrect filing or delayed filing of statutory forms with the Registrar of Companies, some later regularised with additional fees.
The company, its promoters, its group company and its directors are party to legal proceedings, and the filing states an adverse decision could have a material effect.

beats.beat: Specialty chemicals is the part of the chemicals business where a product is made to perform a specific function for a specific buyer, rather than sold as a commodity by the tonne. That distinction is why the growth rates below differ from the wider chemicals industry's.

Scale: CRISIL Research put the Indian chemicals industry excluding pharmaceuticals and fertilisers at ₹5,800–6,200 billion in fiscal 2017, with specialty chemicals (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) at roughly 17% of that, or about ₹1,000 billion.
Growth: the specialty chemicals segment grew 10–12% a year from fiscal 2014 to 2017, and CRISIL Research forecasts 12–14% CAGR ahead.

Within the segment the sub-rates differ: textile chemicals 12%, surfactants 13%, polymer additives 10%, construction chemicals 15%, water chemicals 15%, personal care ingredients 15%, flavours and fragrances 12%.

Demand pools that feed it: paints at ₹401 billion in fiscal 2017, cosmetics and toiletries at ₹430–460 billion, polymer demand growing 9–10% CAGR between fiscals 2017 and 2020, and plastic products 11–13%.

Structure: the industry is highly fragmented, with SMEs holding 70–75% market share, and only a few Indian players have the scale to compete with global majors on product development. That is the field this company competes in.

Demand drivers the filing lists: rising consumption intensity, an Indian middle class projected at 148 million households by 2030, improved consumption standards, a Draft National Chemical Policy aimed at raising chemicals' share of GDP, FDI permitted up to 100%, and China's lower focus on specialty chemicals after stricter environmental rules from 2015.

Headwinds it acknowledges: India's chemicals trade has run a deficit every year from 2012-13 to 2016-17, with imports growing at 6.4% CAGR against exports at 6%; EU-bound exports face the REACH compliance regime; and the filing flags pricing pressure from competition as a risk to revenue and margins.

Rule changes sitting under all of this: GST from July 1, 2017; industrial licensing abolished except for a short list of hazardous chemicals; and four approved Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Regions — Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Odisha — with about ₹9 trillion of proposed investment.

Macro backdrop, kept short because it is context and not company-specific: GDP grew 7.1% in fiscal 2017, private consumption is 58% of GDP, the urban share of population was about 31% in 2011 and is projected at 36% by 2020, and FDI inflows reached $43.5 billion in fiscal 2016.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals processes and sells specialty chemicals — mostly functional additives and chemically modified minerals — and also processes soft minerals and hard minerals. It is a processor, not a miner, and it sells through the network of its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited.

It wants to list on the SME platform of NSE, NSE EMERGE, and the objects of the issue include capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, plus general corporate purposes.
One listed company sits behind it: 20 Microns Limited is named as corporate promoter, and the promoter group holds 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up equity.

Three numbers frame the rest of this report: a ₹1.50 crore profit in FY2015 followed two loss years (₹0.27 crore loss in FY2013, ₹0.12 crore in FY2014); operating cash flow swung to a ₹3.50 crore outflow in FY2017; and the balance sheet totalled ₹34.25 crore at September 30, 2017.
Roadmap sentence: what it sells and how it sells it, the market it sits in, what the offer looks like, six periods of restated numbers, who controls it, and the five risks that matter.

intro.purpose: Orient a reader who has never heard of this company: what it makes, who owns it, where it wants to list, and the three facts that shape the rest of the report.

beats.beat: An SME IPO works the same way as a mainboard one — shares are sold to the public for the first time and then trade on an exchange — but the listing is on a dedicated SME platform, here NSE EMERGE, and the disclosure and eligibility bar is lighter. A fresh issue raises new money for the company; an offer for sale sells existing shares held by a shareholder, and the company receives nothing from that leg.

The objects of the issue, as named: capital expenditure for setting up a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; general corporate purposes; and creating a public trading market for the equity shares by listing on NSE EMERGE to build visibility and brand.
The lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited and the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

What the digest does not carry: the total issue size, the price band, the fresh-issue and offer-for-sale split, the name of any selling shareholder, the bid dates and the lot size. Because the objects include capital expenditure, part of the issue is fresh capital, but the split is not in the facts supplied and must not be inferred.

offer.heading: The offer: what is being sold, and what the money is for
offer.purpose: Explain what an SME IPO on NSE Emerge is, set out the named objects of the issue and the intermediaries, and be explicit that the digest does not carry the issue size, price band or fresh-versus-OFS split.

beats.beat: The cash flow turned negative. After four years of operating inflows, FY2017 produced a ₹3.50 crore operating outflow, and the filing says sustained negative cash flow could affect growth and the business.

Nothing is contracted on either side of the trade. There are no long-term agreements with customers — sales run on purchase orders — and none with raw material suppliers, so neither volume nor price is locked in. Layer on customer concentration of about 59% of revenue from the top 10 customers in FY2017, and the revenue base rests on a small number of repeat buyers with no contractual obligation to return.

One plant may be operating without the full set of permissions. The company states it has not yet obtained certain statutory and regulatory licences, registrations and approvals required to operate the manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, and cannot assure it will not be penalised for the non-compliance.

Legal proceedings involve the company and the people who run it — the company, its promoters, its group company and its directors are all parties, and an adverse decision could materially affect the business.

Control and related-party dealing point the same way. Promoters hold 99.76% pre-issue, so public shareholders would be a small minority with limited ability to influence decisions, and the company has transacted with related parties for each of the last five years and may keep doing so.
